source: generated by tools/build_ownership_manifest.py from d5lib constants + the named Overlord/v1 records; do not hand-edit (the tests fail if it drifts)
notes: One owner per band. 'contested' names two claimants and nothing may be allocated there.
'unallocated' is not free: a claim in an unallocated band is refused, so an unrecorded range cannot be taken by accident.

Overlord bands are reserved for Overlord's content. Under NORTH-STAR.md that content is converted into kit mods, so the numbers are kept free for the conversion rather than for a co-installed Overlord.
Scope: offline. Every band cites a file, a report section or a module constant; nothing here was verified by launching the game.

rules.grandfather: Existing installed packs keep the ids they already have. The manifest records them; it does not move them (see OWNERSHIP-REPORT.md, migration).
rules.not_co_resident: A separately installed Overlord and the kit are not co-resident: unlock flags, mastery slots 47-52 and the 20000-21999 ids are single-owner.

unique_registry_lease.note: A unique character's class id is a registry identity, one rank only (digit 0; 1-5 unused). Its char.dat row id equals the identity because the game finds a class's row by id (char_find_by_id 0x140061f80). Its graphics are keyed to the low physical row it leases (anm band unique_sprite), so it derives no 10000 + id portraits and the class-derived check does not apply. Adding a rank (digit 1-5) turns it into a class family and needs its own band here.

unique_row_lease.note: A unique character carries no family and no registry identity: its class id IS its char.dat row id (d5lib/newchars.py, d5lib/d4unique.check_conflicts), so the unique row band owns the matching class ids. A unique placed outside 223-403 or the re-leased rows 931/941 needs its own band here before a build may claim it.

unlock_flag.description: FlagList indices. The game keeps one flag per class rank (17001..17282 named, FLAG_CHARAMAKE_*); the kit continues the block for its own families.

rules.overlord_claim: Overlord packs 239 unlock slots, three bits each, over the whole 17283..17999 block (a different encoding of the same bits). The kit owns the block: an Overlord class converted into a kit mod leases a kit family and uses the kit's flags. A separately installed Overlord is not co-resident.

mastery_slot.description: Per-unit class-mastery array index (unit + 0x30A4 + 24 * slot + 4 * rank). The game keeps 53 slots; the kit leases the six spare ones to imported families.

bands.label: vanilla class-mastery slots 0-46 (one per native family)
kit leases: mastery_slots.json maps one imported family per spare slot, permanently

rules.overlord_claim: Overlord treats slots 47-51 as one 120-byte packed table and 52 as working state for its own class pool (d5_custom_classes.c:43,106,283). The kit owns all six slots; Overlord's packed pool is not co-resident.
rules.index_range: an index >= 53 is out of range: the game's reader bound is 0x35 (53).

rules.allocation_not_reservation: These ids are allocated first-free from the loaded table (unique characters: 10000 + char id // 10 * 10 + n; classes without one: 13000+), not reserved in advance. A collision is caught when the table is loaded at build time, so this manifest does not model them as derived bands.

personality_id.description: charPersonal.dat row ids. Three rows per imported class family (variant 0..2), found at creation time by voice_group = 100 + (family - 1000) // 10; the id is the table key (the loader sorts on it), so it must be unique across every installed mod.

unique_keyed_graphics.note: A unique character's sprite ids are its char.dat row .. row + 2 and its cut-in / status portrait 10000 + row .. +1 (d5lib/d4unique.py:479, d5lib/newchars.py:7-8). The bands 223-403 and 10223-10404 encode that for the unique row band. A unique on a row whose derived ids leave the band -- rows 402 and 403 derive 404/405, vanilla rows -- is refused by the claims check instead of being silently allocated; move the unique or extend the band deliberately.

rules.family_portraits: A class family's portrait / list-icon set is 10000 + family + 0..9 (ten colours, d5lib/newclasses.py:399-419). That wider window applies to families, not to uniques, so it is modelled by the 11270-12905 band.
